title: Matched annual rain years show a runoff loss but weaker evidence for a rain-slope change in south-east Australia
abstract: We test whether the reported post-1997 loss of rain sensitivity remains in annual rain analogues. We reuse verified CAMELS-AUS v2.03 annual tables. Current and prior-year rain matches use a 0.35 standard-deviation limit, donor reuse and a quadratic correction for residual mismatch. In 123 selected south-east Australian catchments, matched runoff in 2010-2021 was 22.2% below the reference mean (conditional joint 95% interval -31.1% to -14.5%). The slope change was -16.9% of the reference slope. Its spatial interval excluded zero (-31.2% to -5.0%), but the interval with shared annual residual blocks included zero (-37.1% to +3.9%). Tight matches and SILO rain still gave negative joint slope intervals. On 96 shared gauges, omission of 2010-2011 reduced slope loss from 12.7% to 3.9%, while runoff loss stayed at 17.5%. This shows a less stable slope signature than mean loss under this design. It does not prove an unchanged slope or refute tests with different samples and nulls. Limits include annual rain controls only, incomplete overlap, short eras and model-dependent conditional intervals. Code, compatible inputs, provenance, aggregate and per-year evidence, resampling draws and an independent arithmetic audit are supplied.

display.caption: Matched-year slope and mean-flow differences. Lines show conditional 95% intervals with spatial cell and residual block uncertainty. Samples change across tests; block1 and block5 use one- and five-year residual blocks.

citations.reason: Verified annual input data and the reported slope-loss signature.
Earlier low-runoff periods and post-1997 slope loss motivate a test on supported annual rain states.
Prior mean analogue comparison. We extend the question to matched slope changes, shared annual uncertainty and year omission.
